newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 19.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Thursday:

- A group of Marxist guerrillas who took hundreds of international dignitaries hostage in a raid on the Japanese ambassador's residence said they would begin killing them unless the government of Peru agreed to release the rebels' jailed comrades.

- The Clinton Administration disclosed this evening that Charles Yah Lin Trie, the Arkansas businessman who raised hundreds of thousands of dollars in questionable contributions for the Clintons' legal defence fund, went to the White House at least two dozen times in the last four years and was in the Oval Office at least twice.
- A Federal judge overseeing a breast implant case in Oregon has ruled that lawyers cannot introduce evidence saying that implants cause disease, because such evidence is not scientifically valid.

- Tucked into the new school governance bill passed by the New York State Legislature was an eight-line provision in the 24-page measure that came as a surprise to many: the creation of new borough-level deputies in the school bureaucracy.
- An FBI agent was arrested at the agency's training academy on charges that for five years he secretly sold classified information to Moscow in return for $224,000.
